text:
incident-bot: URGENT: Multiple ELB target groups in us-east-1a/us-east-1b returning 502/504s and high connection errors. Auto-alert triggered by 5xx spike > 15% for 10m. Paging on-call now.

maria: i'm on it, joining channel. seeing error spike across both edge and app elbs.

sanjay: pulling metrics — ELB 5xx rate at 18% region-wide, but 1b shows connection reset counts >> 1a.

olivia: getting reports from customer success of a dozen customers with timeouts, CS is flagging high-traffic tenants.

maria: quick triage: checking instance health for target groups.

sanjay: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --region us-east-1` shows many targets in us-east-1b UNHEALTHY with "target: connection reset"

maria: confirmed ENI attach/detach churn in us-east-1b from cloudwatch events, looks like packet loss/MTU errors on a subset of AZ b hosts.

olivia: any idea if Route53 is doing weighted shifts? I see a jump in DNS weighted records for prod-api to other AZs.

rachel: support notified customers and opened status page draft. ETA for full update in 10.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) remove affected targets from ELB target groups, 2) force Route53 weight shift away from affected AZ, 3) enable regional fallback pool (edge-proxy-us-east-2) for heavy tenants. doing step 1 now.

sanjay: i'm running a quick script to drain targets: ```
for tg in $(cat tgs.txt); do aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn $tg --targets Id=i-xxxx --region us-east-1; done
```

olivia: small note — draining will spike load in remaining AZs; autoscaling policies need to uphold. watching queue lengths.

incident-bot: @maria @sanjay @olivia on-call handover in 50m unless incident extended.

maria: update: removed ~30 unhealthy targets in 1b, 5xxs dropped to ~7% in 8m. still seeing elevated latencies for customers pinned to 1b.

sanjay: Route53 weight adjustment applied: shifting 40% traffic off us-east-1b to others: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://shift.json` result: PENDING.

olivia: confirmed pending change propagated at most edge PoPs. early signs show successful reroute for ~60% of queries.

derek: support: which customers to prioritize for seatbelt responses? list attached in support thread. High-traffic tenants A,C,F flagged for priority notifications.

rachel: drafting public status: "Partial disruption to US-East (1b) regional capacity affecting some API requests. We are actively mitigating and routing traffic away from impacted hosts. Customers: no data loss, degraded availability for some tenants." :loudspeaker:

maria: root cause hypothesis: a subset of instances in AZ-b experiencing kernel-level NIC drivers causing MTU fragmentation and TCP RSTs, causing ELB health checks to fail. engineering is collecting syslogs.

sanjay: confirmed unusual MTU ICMP fragmentation logs and some kernel panics on two hosts. opened support ticket with AWS for ENI-level telemetry.

olivia: temporary hardening: enforce smaller MTU on edge proxies in AZ-b to avoid fragmentation until we can patch. pushing config via ansible: `ansible-playbook adjust-mtu.yml -i inventory/us-east-1b`

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in progress. Severity: SEV2. Pager duty escalation level 2.

maria: when Route53 change settles, we should see 80-90% of customer traffic off 1b; watching error rate.

sanjay: AWS replied — they see an underlying hypervisor network interface flapping impacting ENI queueing in us-east-1b. They recommended instance reboot for affected hosts or live-migration. planning controlled reboots.

olivia: scheduling rolling reboot of affected instances with canary, 3 at a time. will hold if autoscaler can't keep up.

maria: canary reboot started on i-0a1 (low traffic tenant). monitoring logs.

olivia: canary looks good, healthchecks restored. starting batch reboots.

derek: support update sent to customers A and C with temporary workarounds (retry/backoff) and notice of failover to other AZs.

rachel: internal note: coordinate with sales for any enterprise customers that need louder comms.

maria: after reboots, ENI metrics stabilized, ELB 5xxs down to 2.1% region-wide. Route53 weight can be partially restored; hold at conservative levels while we verify.

sanjay: final check: no more kernel panics in syslog, packet loss gone on previously affected hosts. AWS marks the host hardware as suspect.

incident-bot: ACTION: begin incident wrap-up checklist. Assign RCA lead and timeline.

maria: I'll own RCA with infra; initial timeline: impact start ~1715001200, mitigation started ~1715001400, major mitigation (reboots + route53 shift) completed ~1715004200.

olivia: add follow-ups: 1) host kernel driver downgrade/patch, 2) add ENI-level health alarms to detect MTU/ICMP frag errors earlier, 3) Route53 automated weight rollback playbook.

derek: CS will send follow-up notes to affected customers and offer dedicated conference bridge for top-tier tenants.

rachel: handoff: @sanjay will be primary on-call for next 2h to confirm stability. leaving channel. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: acknowledged. I'll monitor for 2h and escalate if anything recurs.

pagerduty: On-call change: @sanjay acknowledged incident at 1715004300.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): Traffic shifted and problematic hosts rebooted. Monitoring for 1h before Postmortem.

maria: thanks everyone. creating PM notes now and will file full postmortem with logs + timeline + customer impact table.

olivia: adding perf graphs and the exact CLI commands used to the postmortem.

rachel: status page updated to resolved with follow-up link.

derek: closing customer threads after follow-up comms.

maria: final: recommend increasing cross-AZ capacity slack for next 6h and schedule kernel-driver patch window this week.
